title: Beylik of Sinop
capsule: In this 1305–1333 phase, the Beylik of Sinop was the fledgling Candarid principality on the Black Sea, where Süleyman I Pasha's family wrested the port of Sinop from its Pervaneid rulers by the mid-1320s. Ruling under nominal Ilkhanid Mongol suzerainty, it functioned as a contested trade hub frequented by the Genoese, predating the dynastic strife of the 1330s–80s that later split the realm.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The beylik's territorial footprint is only approximately attested; boundaries are inferred from Ottoman administrative records and Byzantine sources, with no surviving contemporary maps.
